must_remember: Work is defined mathematically as the line integral of force along a displacement path: $W = \int \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r}$.
For a constant force, $W = Fs \cos\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the force and displacement vectors.
A force is conservative if the work done by it along a closed path is zero or independent of the path.
The relationship between a conservative force field and potential energy is given by $\vec{F} = -\nabla U$.
The net work done on a particle by all forces equals the change in its kinetic energy: $W_{\text{net}} = \Delta K = K_f - K_i$.
Instantaneous power is defined as the scalar product of force and velocity: $P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v}$.
Mechanical energy is conserved only when no non-conservative forces like friction do work.

glossary.meaning: The energy transferred to or from an object via the application of force along a displacement, measured in Joules.
A force for which work done is independent of path and depends only on initial and final positions.
States that the net work done by all forces acting on a body equals its change in kinetic energy.
The rate at which work is done or energy is transferred, measured in Watts ($J/s$).
A force, such as kinetic friction, that dissipates mechanical energy into non-recoverable thermal energy.
